ceterms:description.en-US: The reduction of power consumption is rapidly becoming one of the key issues in digital system design. Traditionally, digital system design has mainly focused on performance and area trade-offs. This course will provide a thorough introduction to digital design for lower consumption at the circuit, logic, and architectural level. Graduate degree credit will not be given for both CSCE 42303 and CSCE 52303. Prerequisite: CSCE 22104 with a grade of C or better or graduate standing in Computer Science Computer Engineering (CSCE) or graduate standing in Electrical Engineering (ELEG). (Typically offered: Irregular)

languageModel.name: qwen3.5:9b
languageModel.argument: The sentence begins with 'CSCE 22104', which is a course code, followed by 'with a grade of C or better'. These two are joined by the word 'or', indicating that either taking the course OR having the specific grade satisfies the condition. According to the CTDL definition of ceterms:alternativeCondition ('...from which any one path fulfills the parent condition'), this forms an 'any_of' node containing the course and the text condition. The second part of the sentence, 'graduate standing in Computer Science Computer Engineering (CSCE) or graduate standing in Electrical Engineering (ELEG)', contains two distinct conditions joined by 'or'. Since only one of these standing requirements is needed to satisfy that sub-group, this forms a nested 'any_of' node containing two text items. The outer structure remains an 'any_of' because the initial course/grade option and the graduate standing options are alternatives to each other.
